subject.title: fix: serialize outbound deliveries per channel+recipient

question: Should this draft be reworked in place, replaced with a narrower maintainer-owned fix, or intentionally accepted with the same-lane blocking tradeoff?
rationale: The bug is proven, but the patch changes the message-delivery boundary and can still misorder or wedge sends unless maintainers choose the lane and stalled-send semantics.

options.title: Repair the lane boundary first
options.body: Move serialization to a canonical, collision-safe lane before write-ahead enqueue and reuse or deliberately extend the existing keyed queue primitive.

options.title: Accept same-lane blocking deliberately
options.body: Maintainers could accept per-recipient head-of-line blocking only after adding or documenting bounded stalled-send behavior.

options.title: Replace the draft
options.body: If the branch is not worth reworking, close or pause this draft and keep the demonstrated ordering bug for a narrower replacement PR.

recommendation.title: Repair the lane boundary first
recommendation.body: Move serialization to a canonical, collision-safe lane before write-ahead enqueue and reuse or deliberately extend the existing keyed queue primitive.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history across outbound delivery and plugin boundary refactors touched by the decision.
